newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria economy weak in Q1 says central bank.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria economy weak in Q1 says central bank.

text.p: Key sectors of Nigeria's economy failed to record the expected growth in the first quarter of this year, the central bank said in a report on Wednesday.
"In spite of efforts to sustain a stable macro-economic environment and stimulate growth, available information shows that overall performance of the economy was mixed," it said.

"Activities in the real sector in the review period remained weak mainly as a result of incessant power failure, and recurrent shortages of petroleum products which tended to increase costs and disrupt production," it added.

The report is broadly inline with expert opinion that the level of gross domestic product (gdp) growth needed to put Nigeria's economy on a recovery path has not materialised in the first half of the year.

A recent business survey showed employment had worsened, consumer purchasing power has fallen and the oil industry, Nigeria's economic engine is reeling from lack of government funding while a persistent fuel shortage threatened an industrial crisis.
"The prospects for improved real sector performance in the rest of 1997 are uncertain," the central bank report said.
"The attainment of 5.0 percent growth target depends on the ability of the authorities to sustain the existing stable macro-economic environment," it added.
Africa's most populous nation has been in crisis since the army annulled the 1993 presidential vote.
The central bank said manufacturing capacity utilisation was 34.2 percent in the first quarter, a decline of 0.3 percent from the last quarter of 1996.
The main good news was on declining inflation.
"Inflationary pressures continued to moderate, considerably falling from 29.3 percent in December, 1996 to 22.2 percent at the end of March, 1997," the central bank said.
"The possibility of acheiving the 15 percent inflation target by December 1997 remains feasible," it added.
Finance minister Anthony Ani said last week April inflation was down to 18.5 percent, but official sources say the actual level is closer to 21.4 percent.
